marketSession: Asian morning; before Monday's US regular stock-market session
title: Oil is pulling back. The bigger risk has not gone away.
intro: Brent fell to around $103.35 a barrel in early Monday trading. Traders are hoping more Russian diesel will reach the market, but neither Russia nor Ukraine has confirmed the proposed energy ceasefire. For now, I would treat this as some relief in oil prices, not proof that the fuel shortage has ended.

sections.label: AI & STOCKS
sections.text: Nasdaq futures were up around 0.5% in the same early snapshot. That looks encouraging, but I would not ignore the cost of funding the AI boom. TSMC's September sales rose 54.6% from a year ago, while some companies building data centres still need to borrow heavily. Strong chip demand and financing problems can exist at the same time.

sections.label: US YIELDS & THE DOLLAR
sections.text: The US 10-year Treasury yield last closed at 5.24% on Friday. US bond markets are observing a Monday holiday, so we do not yet know whether the pullback in oil will bring borrowing costs down. The dollar is also holding near recent highs. I would want to see both yields and the dollar soften before calling this a broader relief rally.

sections.label: WHAT I AM WATCHING
sections.text: Wednesday's US CPI and Thursday's PPI will test whether inflation pressure is easing. TSMC's quarterly results on Thursday will also help show whether strong AI chip sales are translating into solid profits. If oil stays lower and tech shares strengthen without credit getting worse, that would support the rally. If energy prices rebound and borrowing costs rise, I would be much more cautious.

verdict: For now, the market has a reason to bounce, but not yet enough evidence for an all-clear.
dataLimits: Brent, Nasdaq futures and dollar references are early 12 October snapshots, not live quotes. The Treasury yield is from Friday 9 October. No confirmed Monday US cash-market close is included.
